Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old male with 1.5–2 months of intermittent transient right upper limb paresthesia and weakness with episodic ipsilateral lower limb weakness and gait change; working diagnosis communicated as transient ischemic attacks (TIA) with urgent referral to a TIA clinic arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Intermittent "pins and needles" (paresthesia) and numbness of the right hand with transient right arm weakness.
  - Associated transient weakness of the leg and episodes of abnormal gait occurring concurrently with the arm/hand symptoms.
  - Generalized fatigue, episodic nausea, decreased motivation/energy.
  - Recent difficulty holding a cup and slight difficulty drinking during the episodes (reported over the last couple of days).
  - Sensation of "something in my throat" during episodes.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~1.5–2 months ago.
  - Initial symptom: brief period (a couple of days) of tiredness, then returned to baseline.
  - Neurological episodes initially occurred approximately once monthly to once weekly; frequency has increased and now occurs a couple of times per day.
  - Each neurological episode lasts a few days (patient reports 3–4 days) then resolves back to normal.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - None specifically identified in the consultation.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Fatigue and intermittent nausea.
  - No current difficulty swallowing (but a throat sensation reported during episodes).
  - No speech disturbance reported during episodes.
  - No visual disturbances reported (patient wears glasses; no change reported).
  - No continuous symptoms at time of consultation (asymptomatic during consult).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No ongoing dysphagia at time of consult.
  - No speech impairment reported.
  - No reported visual change during episodes.
  - No other chronic illnesses reported by patient.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Prior screening (timing not specified) after father's vascular procedure: blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes testing reportedly normal.
- Medications:
  - Aspirin 75 mg once daily (self-initiated; started after father's operation). Route not specified.
- Allergies:
  - Penicillin allergy only.

Social History:
- Occupation: medical doctor, specialty in plastic surgery.
- Lives with wife.
- Tobacco: Denies smoking.
- Alcohol/substance use: Not documented in transcript.
- No other social, occupational, or financial factors discussed.

Family History:
- Father: underwent "an operation to the side of his neck to reduce the risk of stroke" (no procedure name or date provided).

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (video lost; clinician could not see patient).

Investigations:
- No investigations completed at time of consult.
- Planned/anticipated investigations per referral:
  - Carotid artery ultrasound (carotid Doppler/ultrasound).
  - Brain imaging (may include CT scan) to exclude intracranial bleed or acute pathology.
  - Further rapid assessment at TIA clinic with additional tests as indicated.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1:
  - Assessment: Transient ischemic attack (TIA) / mini-stroke suspected based on recurrent transient focal neurological deficits (right hand paresthesia/numbness, right arm weakness, transient leg weakness and gait disturbance), increasing in frequency.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent referral to TIA clinic arranged; expected contact within 1–2 days (clinician noted usual turnaround aiming for being seen within next 1–2 days, by Thursday/Friday given day of consult).
    - TIA clinic to perform carotid ultrasound and likely brain imaging and other assessments to exclude stroke/TIA.
    - Patient advised that if symptoms return and are prolonged or persistent (consistent with possible stroke), go to Emergency Department immediately.
    - Patient advised to contact the practice if there is any delay in being contacted by the hospital or if symptoms recur; telephone assessment available.
    - Hospital contact options (PALS and TIA clinic numbers) to be recorded in the consultation notes for patient to chase appointment.
- Issue 2:
  - Assessment: Current aspirin 75 mg daily being taken by patient without prior GP prescription or discussion.
  - Plan:
    - No specific change documented during consult; aspirin use recorded and will be available to hospital/TIA clinic review.
    - Recommend that aspirin use be reviewed by receiving clinic/GP (noted that GP had not been informed previously).
- Issue 3:
  - Assessment: Family history of carotid/vascular intervention (father); prior vascular risk screening reportedly normal.
  - Plan:
    - TIA clinic assessment will include risk factor review and targeted investigations (blood tests, imaging) as per clinic protocols.
- General plan items:
  - Referral sent immediately.
  - Patient instructed to contact TIA clinic/PALS to ensure appointment is booked and to contact the GP service if issues arise.
  - Clear safety-netting: attend A&E for prolonged/persistent symptoms suggesting stroke.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No formal vital signs recorded (heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - No focused neurological examination documented (cranial nerves, motor strength, coordination, sensory exam).
  - No full medication reconciliation beyond aspirin; other regular medications not documented (patient denied other medications).
  - No dates for prior blood tests or details of results beyond "all OK" as reported by patient.
  - No imaging or laboratory results available at time of consult.
  - No documentation of alcohol use or substance use.
  - Date of birth not provided; age documented as 32 years.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio/video connection intermittently poor; clinician noted loss of video and occasional poor connection but overall history elements were obtained and intelligible.
